title: Smallest String From Allowed Swaps
statement:
You get a lowercase string s and a list pairs of index pairs [a, b]. A move swaps the characters at positions a and b for one of the given pairs. You may make any number of moves, using any pair as often as you like.

Return the alphabetically smallest string you can reach.

examples.why: Positions 0 and 3 trade t and b; positions 1 and 2 trade k and e. Each group sorts on its own: "bekt".
There is no pair [0, 2], but swaps can chain through position 1, so all three positions mix freely.
No moves at all, so the string stays as it is.

constraints: s has only lowercase English letters
hints: If a can swap with b and b can swap with c, can the characters at a and c end up anywhere among those three positions?
Positions joined by pairs, directly or through a chain, form a group. Inside a group, any arrangement is reachable.
Find the groups with union-find (or DFS), sort each group's characters, and write them back into that group's positions in increasing index order.

explain.intuition:
Look at the pairs as edges between positions. Swaps along a chain of edges can move any character to any position in the same connected group: adjacent swaps are enough to sort a whole list, as bubble sort shows. So inside a group, every arrangement is reachable, and positions in different groups never trade.

That makes the answer local: for each group, put its smallest character at its smallest index, the next smallest at the next index, and so on. Union-find builds the groups in near-linear time.
steps: Create a union-find over positions 0 … n − 1 and union every pair.
Group positions by their root. Positions are visited in increasing order, so each group's list is already sorted.
For each group, collect its characters and sort them.
Write the sorted characters back into the group's positions in order, and join the result.
pitfalls: Only applying each given swap once when it helps. In "zyx" with pairs [0, 1], [1, 2] that misses the chain through position 1.
Sorting the whole string. Positions in different groups can never exchange characters.
Union-find without path compression on a long chain of pairs, which makes each find O(n).

solutions.title: Flood fill from every position
solutions.idea: For each position, run a fresh search over the pairs to find everything it connects to, then use its rank inside the sorted group.

solutions.title: Union-find, then sort each group
solutions.idea: Union the paired positions, bucket positions by root, sort each bucket's characters and write them back in index order.

followups: Return the largest string instead. What changes?
Each swap now costs 1 and you want the smallest string reachable with at most k swaps. Why does the grouping idea stop working?
